notes:
suite: Full relevant test suite = repository's complete registered ctest collection (75 ONNX operator tests, tests/op/test_onnx_op_*.cpp, Tengine CPU reference backend) + CUDA-backend on-GPU parity harness (9 ImageNet-style models). Completeness-correction re-run (v3): with onnx 1.22.0 now installed, the required ONNX node test data was generated and all 75 op tests were actually executed (they reach inference).
scope_note: PART A (75 ctest onnx op tests) runs on the Tengine CPU REFERENCE backend via create_graph(nullptr,...) and does NOT exercise the CUDA backend (out of strict CUDA migration scope); they are nonetheless executed for real per the completeness rule. PART B (9 models via tm_classification_cuda) is the portion that actually exercises the migrated CUDA backend. Data for the 75 op tests was produced from the installed onnx package's ONNX backend node conformance data (onnx/backend/test/data/node/) converted to Tengine .tmfile with Tengine's own convert_tool; 10 ops whose stock models use opset-25 (axes/pads moved to inputs) or omit a required attr were regenerated at a Tengine-parseable opset (see regen_hard_ops.py).
onnx_op_ctest_result: 75 ONNX op tests executed on the CPU reference backend: 68 passed, 7 failed (raw ctest exit=8, 91% passed). The 7 failures are pre-existing Tengine CPU-reference-backend defects, NOT CoreX/CUDA and NOT missing data (all reach inference): 4 conv tests (basic_conv_with_padding, basic_conv_without_padding, conv_with_strides_no_padding, conv_with_strides_padding) output all-zeros because the harness fills the weight buffer (input_1) AFTER prerun_graph, so Tengine prepacks zero conv weights; batchnorm_example -> 'free(): invalid size' abort at teardown; dropout_default -> computes correctly ('test pass') then aborts with heap corruption ('register_batchnorm_ref_op() failed' / 'free(): invalid next size'); pad_reflect -> 'double free or corruption' abort at teardown. Full per-case output in test.log PART A2.
